               data above to determine which categories of failure triggered this run,
               then follow the matching workflow(s) in AGENTS.md:
               - Test failures → "Write a PR For A Failing Test"
               - Unmarked slow tests → "Mark Slow Tests"
               - Unmarked docker tests → "Mark Docker Tests"

               Use 'gh run view' if failure data is empty or more context is required.

            3. **Overrides.** You are running in CI, not interactively. Apply these
               overrides to whichever AGENTS.md workflow(s) you follow:
               - **Branch name:** `agent/fix-ci-${{ github.run_number }}`
               - **Linting:** Run `make check` and fix any issues.
               - **PR:** Create a **non-draft** pull request (overrides the usual
                 `--draft` convention) with:
                 - Title: brief description of what was fixed.
                 - Body: link to the source run URL.
                 - Include: "Reviewers: use 'Request changes' to trigger an automatic follow-up fix."
                 - Label: `automated-heavy-test-fix`.
                 - **Mandatory:** Include the full checklist from
                   `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` verbatim in the PR body.
                   The `Check PR template` CI job greps for the literal checklist
                   substrings and fails the PR otherwise — this applies to bot PRs
                   too. Mark each item with `— No.` (or appropriate brief answer).
                 - Under "Related issue", write
                   `Closes: no linked issue as this fixes a failing scheduled test run`
                   (or `Closes: #<number>` if an issue tracks the failure). The
                   same CI job fails without a `Closes:` line.

            4. **Git commit messages.** Use a plain single-line `-m` string. Do NOT
               include `\n` newlines, `Co-Authored-By` trailers, command substitution
               like `$(...)`, or backticks — Claude Code blocks commands containing
               newlines as a security measure (a newline in a shell command can hide
               injected commands).

          claude_args: |
            --model ${{ steps.setup.outputs.claude_model }} --allowedTools "Bash(git *),Bash(gh *),Bash(uv run *),Bash(make *),Bash(python *),Bash(ls *),Bash(mkdir *),Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep,WebFetch,WebSearch"
          show_full_output: true

      - name: Notify Slack on timeout
        if: cancelled()
        env:
          # SECURITY: FAILING_RUN_URL is untrusted (from dispatch payload); jq builds the JSON
          # so contents are escaped, and the webhook secret is in env not on the CLI.
          # zizmor: template-injection (https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#template-injection)
          FAILING_RUN_URL: ${{ steps.context.outputs.run_url }}
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          RUN_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          payload=$(jq -nc \
            --arg failing "$FAILING_RUN_URL" \
            --arg run "$RUN_URL" \
            '{
              text: "⚠️ Claude Fix Tests cancelled (fix-from-ci)",
              blocks: [{
                type: "section",
                text: {
                  type: "mrkdwn",
                  text: ("*⚠️ Claude Fix Tests cancelled*\n\nThe `fix-from-ci` job exceeded its 60-minute limit or was cancelled manually and did not complete.\n\n*Failing run:* <" + $failing + "|View Failing Run>\n*This run:* <" + $run + "|View Claude Run>")
                }
              }]
            }')
          curl -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
            --data "$payload" \
            "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL"

  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Job 2: Address review feedback on automated-heavy-test-fix PRs
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  fix-from-review:
    name: Fix failing tests from PR review
    # Yield to fix-pr (claude-issue-solver.yaml) when the maintainer
    # explicitly types /claude in the review body — that's an opt-in for
    # the broader /claude workflow. Without /claude, fix-from-review keeps
    # its original contract for automated-*-fix PRs.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request_review'
      && github.event.review.state == 'changes_requested'
      && !startsWith(github.event.review.body, '/claude')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read         # list prior runs to dedupe Claude triggers on the same PR
      id-token: write       # AWS OIDC for Claude on Bedrock via aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials
    concurrency:
      group: claude-fix-review-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: true

    steps:
      - name: Validate PR and reviewer
        id: validate
        uses: actions/github-script@3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3 # v9.0.0
        with:
          script: |
            const pr = context.payload.pull_request;
            const review = context.payload.review;

            // Check PR has an automated-*-fix label (e.g. automated-heavy-test-fix, automated-smoke-test-fix, automated-issue-fix)
            const hasLabel = pr.labels.some(l =>
              /^automated-.*-fix$/.test(l.name)
            );
            if (!hasLabel) {
              core.info('PR does not have an automated-*-fix label — skipping');
              core.setOutput('skip', 'true');
              return;
            }

            // Check reviewer has write or admin permission
            const { data: permData } = await github.rest.repos.getCollaboratorPermissionLevel({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              username: review.user.login,
            });
            const perm = permData.permission;
            if (perm !== 'write' && perm !== 'admin') {
              core.info(`Reviewer ${review.user.login} has permission ${perm} — skipping`);
              core.setOutput('skip', 'true');
              return;
            }

            core.setOutput('skip', 'false');
            core.setOutput('pr_number', pr.number.toString());
            core.setOutput('pr_head_ref', pr.head.ref);

      # Use a GitHub App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so that pushes to the PR
      # branch re-trigger CI — commits pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN are silently
      # ignored by downstream `on: pull_request` workflows. Permissions come
      # from the App's installation settings, not from this workflow.
      - name: Generate App token
        if: steps.validate.outputs.skip != 'true'
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Scope the token to what these jobs exercise (push commits/branches,
          # open and update PRs, comment on issues/PRs). Without an explicit
          # permission-* input the token inherits the App installation's full
          # permission set.
          permission-contents: write
          permission-pull-requests: write
          permission-issues: write

      - name: Checkout
        if: steps.validate.outputs.skip != 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ steps.validate.outputs.pr_head_ref }}
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          persist-credentials: false

      # Snapshot the PR's CI status for the Claude prompt below.
      # Outputs consumed by the `Run Claude Code to address review` step:
      #   - steps.checks.outputs.status — one word: passing | pending | failing
      #   - /tmp/PR_CHECKS.txt          — full `gh pr checks` output
      # Status is derived from `gh pr checks` exit code:
      # 0 = all passing, 8 = some still pending/in-progress, anything else = failing.
      # Claude uses these to decide whether to drill into failures with
      # `gh run view --log-failed` or check-run annotation APIs.
      - name: Fetch PR checks
        id: checks
        if: steps.validate.outputs.skip != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ steps.validate.outputs.pr_number }}
        run: |
          set +e
          gh pr checks "$PR_NUMBER" > /tmp/PR_CHECKS.txt 2>&1
          rc=$?
          set -e
          case "$rc" in
            0) status=passing ;;
            8) status=pending ;;
            *) status=failing ;;
          esac
          echo "status=$status" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "rc=$rc"         >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Checks status: $status (rc=$rc)"

      # The composite action at .github/actions/claude-setup/action.yaml is
      # resolved against the workspace, which is the PR-checked-out tree.
      # Restore it from origin/main as defence-in-depth, so the
      # AWS-OIDC-configuring action.yaml always comes from trusted source.
      # Fail-closed: any failure here aborts before Claude runs. See #1687.
      - name: Restore trusted claude-setup action
        if: steps.validate.outputs.skip != 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p .github/actions/claude-setup
          git show origin/main:.github/actions/claude-setup/action.yaml \
            > .github/actions/claude-setup/action.yaml

      # workflow-security: allow sync-on-pr-checkout - The fix agent requires the pull request dependency set. Capability separation is tracked in https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_evals/issues/2201.
      - name: Setup
        if: steps.validate.outputs.skip != 'true'
        id: setup
        uses: ./.github/actions/claude-setup
        with:
          skip_checkout: "true"
          role_arn: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_ROLE_ARN }}

      # workflow-security: allow agent-unrestricted-file-read - Shell access is required to modify and test fixes. Capability separation is tracked in https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_evals/issues/2201.
      - name: Run Claude Code to address review
        if: steps.validate.outputs.skip != 'true'
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@61a9c274fa7110a66dfafc1bbbced03833eb25fe # v1.0.269
        with:
          use_bedrock: true
          github_token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          prompt: |
            You are an autonomous CI-fix agent. A reviewer has requested changes on PR #${{ steps.validate.outputs.pr_number }}.

            PR CI status at workflow start: ${{ steps.checks.outputs.status }} (one of: passing, pending, failing)
            PR check details: /tmp/PR_CHECKS.txt (`gh pr checks` output — glyphs: ✓ pass, X fail, * pending, - skipped)

            ## Instructions

            1. Read ALL review comments:
               - `gh pr view ${{ steps.validate.outputs.pr_number }} --comments`
               - `gh api repos/${{ github.repository }}/pulls/${{ steps.validate.outputs.pr_number }}/comments` (for inline code comments)
            2. If the CI status above is `failing`, read `/tmp/PR_CHECKS.txt` to see which checks failed. For any failure relevant to this fix PR, drill in:
               - Extract the numeric run id from the end of the row's URL and run `gh run view <run_id> --log-failed` to get the actual error message or stack trace.
               - If structured annotations are needed instead, use `gh api repos/${{ github.repository }}/commits/<head_sha>/check-runs` to look up check-run IDs, then `gh api repos/${{ github.repository }}/check-runs/<id>/annotations`.
               If the status is `pending`, some checks are still running — don't assume they'll fail, but note in your PR comment if you're merging before they complete.
            <EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
            Here are some examples of things that you MUST NEVER DO:
            - DO NOT make the test pass by downgrading the error to a warning, without fixing the original issue!
            - DO NOT attempt to patch the issue locally in the eval, when the issue is actually with the testing pipeline!
            - DO NOT delete any tests!
            - DO NOT begin fixing the issue until you have identified the root cause! Enumerate the steps to reproduce the error that demonstrate that you understand it, and always provide this in the PR description.
            - Use code comments sparingly, do not reference past code in the comments you make.
            </EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
            3. Address EACH piece of feedback from the reviewer and any failed checks that are relevant to this automated fix PR.
            4. Run `make check` and fix any issues.
            5. Commit your changes with a descriptive message referencing the review.
               Use a plain single-line `-m` string. Do NOT include `\n` newlines,
               `Co-Authored-By` trailers, command substitution like `$(...)`, or
               backticks — Claude Code blocks commands containing newlines as a
               security measure.
            6. Push to the current branch.
            7. Comment on the PR summarizing what you changed in response to the review.

          claude_args: |
            --model ${{ steps.setup.outputs.claude_model }} --allowedTools "Bash(git *),Bash(gh *),Bash(uv run *),Bash(make *),Bash(python *),Bash(ls *),Bash(mkdir *),Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep,WebFetch,WebSearch"
          show_full_output: true

      - name: Notify Slack on timeout
        if: cancelled()
        env:
          # SECURITY: jq builds the Slack JSON (proper escaping); webhook secret in env not on the CLI.
          # zizmor: template-injection (https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#template-injection)
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ steps.validate.outputs.pr_number }}
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          RUN_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          PR_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pull/${PR_NUMBER}"
          payload=$(jq -nc \
            --arg pr_number "$PR_NUMBER" \
            --arg pr_url "$PR_URL" \
            --arg run "$RUN_URL" \
            '{
              text: "⚠️ Claude Fix Tests cancelled (fix-from-review)",
              blocks: [{
                type: "section",
                text: {
                  type: "mrkdwn",
                  text: ("*⚠️ Claude Fix Tests cancelled*\n\nThe `fix-from-review` job exceeded its 60-minute limit or was cancelled manually and did not complete.\n\n*PR:* <" + $pr_url + "|#" + $pr_number + ">\n*This run:* <" + $run + "|View Claude Run>")
                }
              }]
            }')
          curl -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
            --data "$payload" \
            "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL"

  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Job 3: Parse smoke-test failures into a matrix
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  parse-smoke-failures:
    name: Parse smoke test failures
    if: >-
      github.event.action == 'smoke-test-failure'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.smoke_failing_evals != '')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.matrix }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.run_url }}

    steps:
      - name: Parse failing evals from payload
        id: parse
        uses: actions/github-script@3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3 # v9.0.0
        env:
          INPUT_SMOKE_FAILING_EVALS: ${{ inputs.smoke_failing_evals }}
          INPUT_RUN_URL: ${{ inputs.run_url }}
        with:
          script: |
            // SECURITY: Eval names from dispatch payloads are attacker-controllable; used downstream
            // in concurrency keys, branch names, PR titles, Claude prompts, and Slack JSON.
            // zizmor: template-injection (https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#template-injection)
            const EVAL_NAME_RE = /^[a-z0-9_]+$/;
            const EVAL_NAME_MAX = 64;
            const EVAL_COUNT_MAX = 10;

            let runUrl, rawEvals;
            if (context.eventName === 'workflow_dispatch') {
              // Manual testing path: parse comma-separated eval names
              runUrl = process.env.INPUT_RUN_URL || 'manual-dispatch';
              rawEvals = (process.env.INPUT_SMOKE_FAILING_EVALS || '')
                .split(',')
                .map(s => s.trim())
                .filter(s => s.length > 0);
            } else {
              const payload = context.payload.client_payload || {};
              runUrl = typeof payload.run_url === 'string' ? payload.run_url : 'unknown';
              rawEvals = Array.isArray(payload.failing_evals) ? payload.failing_evals : [];
            }

            const invalid = [];
            const evals = [];
            for (const candidate of rawEvals) {
              if (typeof candidate !== 'string'
                  || candidate.length === 0
                  || candidate.length > EVAL_NAME_MAX
                  || !EVAL_NAME_RE.test(candidate)) {
                invalid.push(candidate);
              } else {
                evals.push(candidate);
              }
            }

            if (invalid.length > 0) {
              // Fail closed: do not start matrix jobs with any tainted name in scope.
              core.setFailed(
                `Rejected eval name(s) not matching ${EVAL_NAME_RE} (max ${EVAL_NAME_MAX} chars): ` +
                JSON.stringify(invalid),
              );
              return;
            }

            // Cap at EVAL_COUNT_MAX evals to avoid excessive parallel jobs
            if (evals.length > EVAL_COUNT_MAX) {
              core.warning(`Received ${evals.length} failing evals, capping at ${EVAL_COUNT_MAX}`);
              evals.length = EVAL_COUNT_MAX;
            }

            core.setOutput('run_url', runUrl);
            core.setOutput('matrix', JSON.stringify(evals));
            core.info(`Run URL: ${runUrl}`);
            core.info(`Failing evals (${evals.length}): ${JSON.stringify(evals)}`);

  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Job 4: Fix each smoke-test failure (one job per eval)
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  fix-smoke-failure:
    name: Fix smoke test failure
    needs: parse-smoke-failures
    if: needs.parse-smoke-failures.outputs.matrix != '[]'
    strategy:
      matrix:
        eval: ${{ fromJson(needs.parse-smoke-failures.outputs.matrix) }}
      fail-fast: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read         # `gh run view`/`gh run download` to inspect failing smoke runs
      id-token: write       # AWS OIDC for Claude on Bedrock via aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials
    concurrency:
      group: claude-fix-smoke-${{ matrix.eval }}
      cancel-in-progress: true

    steps:
      # Use a GitHub App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so that PRs opened by this
      # job trigger CI — PRs created with GITHUB_TOKEN don't fire downstream
      # `on: pull_request` workflows. Permissions come from the App's
      # installation settings, not from this workflow's `permissions:` block.
      - name: Generate App token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Scope the token to what these jobs exercise (push commits/branches,
          # open and update PRs, comment on issues/PRs). Without an explicit
          # permission-* input the token inherits the App installation's full
          # permission set.
          permission-contents: write
          permission-pull-requests: write
          permission-issues: write

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Check for existing fix PR for this eval
        id: dedup
        uses: actions/github-script@3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3 # v9.0.0
        env:
          # SECURITY: Validated to /^[a-z0-9_]+$/ upstream, but env-passing is the
          # standard mitigation pattern for github-script regardless.
          # zizmor: template-injection (https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#template-injection)
          MATRIX_EVAL: ${{ matrix.eval }}
        with:
          github-token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          script: |
            const { data: prs } = await github.rest.pulls.list({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              state: 'open',
              per_page: 100,
            });
            const evalName = process.env.MATRIX_EVAL;
            const fixPRs = prs.filter(pr =>
              pr.labels.some(l => l.name === 'automated-smoke-test-fix')
              && (pr.title.toLowerCase().includes(evalName.toLowerCase())
                  || pr.head.ref.includes(evalName))
            );
            if (fixPRs.length > 0) {
              const urls = fixPRs.map(pr => `#${pr.number}: ${pr.title}`).join('\n');
              core.info(`Found open fix PRs for ${evalName}:\n${urls}`);
              core.setOutput('skip', 'true');
            } else {
              core.setOutput('skip', 'false');
            }

      - name: Setup
        if: steps.dedup.outputs.skip != 'true'
        id: setup
        uses: ./.github/actions/claude-setup
        with:
          role_arn: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_ROLE_ARN }}
          skip_checkout: "true"

      # workflow-security: allow agent-unrestricted-file-read - Shell access is required to modify and test fixes. Capability separation is tracked in https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_evals/issues/2201.
      - name: Run Claude Code to fix smoke failure
        if: steps.dedup.outputs.skip != 'true'
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@61a9c274fa7110a66dfafc1bbbced03833eb25fe # v1.0.269
        with:
          use_bedrock: true
          github_token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          prompt: |
            You are an autonomous CI-fix agent. Read AGENTS.md for general repo context,
            then follow the "Fix A Failing Smoke Test" workflow in the ci-maintenance-workflow skill.

            ## Context

            A nightly smoke test (--limit 0) found that the eval `${{ matrix.eval }}` is failing.

            Smoke test run: ${{ needs.parse-smoke-failures.outputs.run_url }}

            ## Instructions

            Follow the "Fix A Failing Smoke Test" workflow. The skill's "Hard rules"
            and "Reporting" sections are authoritative — in particular: reproduce
            before fixing, verify after fixing, never skip/xfail/disable the eval as
            a "fix", and if you can't reproduce / can't verify / can't fix, raise a
            **draft** PR using the structured body (the skill's PR Description
            section already specifies the fields). Do not silently abandon the run.

            <EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
            Here are some examples of things that you MUST NEVER DO:
            - DO NOT make the test pass by downgrading the error to a warning, without fixing the original issue!
            - DO NOT attempt to patch the issue locally in the eval, when the issue is actually with the testing pipeline!
            - DO NOT delete any tests!
            - DO NOT begin fixing the issue until you have identified the root cause! Enumerate the steps to reproduce the error that demonstrate that you understand it, and always provide this in the PR description.
            - Use code comments sparingly, do not reference past code in the comments you make.
            </EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
            
            Apply these **overrides** to the workflow:

            1. **Branch name:** `agent/fix-smoke-${{ matrix.eval }}-${{ github.run_number }}`
            2. **Linting:** Run `make check` and fix any issues.
            3. **PR:** Create the PR as **non-draft** when you have a verified fix,
               or **draft** when you are following the skill's blocked-PR path
               (couldn't reproduce / couldn't verify / couldn't fix). Either way:
               - Title: brief description of what was fixed (or "blocked: <reason>" for the draft path) for `${{ matrix.eval }}`.
               - Body: the structured PR description format from the skill's "PR Description" section, plus a link to the smoke test run URL.
               - Include: "Reviewers: use 'Request changes' to trigger an automatic follow-up fix."
               - Label: `automated-smoke-test-fix`.
            4. **Git commit messages.** Use a plain single-line `-m` string. Do NOT
               include `\n` newlines, `Co-Authored-By` trailers, command substitution
               like `$(...)`, or backticks — Claude Code blocks commands containing
               newlines as a security measure (a newline in a shell command can hide
               injected commands).

          claude_args: |
            --model ${{ steps.setup.outputs.claude_model }} --allowedTools "Bash(git *),Bash(gh *),Bash(uv run *),Bash(make *),Bash(python *),Bash(ls *),Bash(mkdir *),Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep,WebFetch,WebSearch"
          show_full_output: true

      - name: Notify Slack on timeout
        if: cancelled() && steps.dedup.outputs.skip != 'true'
        env:
          # SECURITY: MATRIX_EVAL is validated to /^[a-z0-9_]+$/ upstream;
          # SMOKE_RUN_URL is untrusted (dispatch payload) and JSON-escaped below with jq.
          # zizmor: template-injection (https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#template-injection)
          MATRIX_EVAL: ${{ matrix.eval }}
          SMOKE_RUN_URL: ${{ needs.parse-smoke-failures.outputs.run_url }}
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          RUN_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          payload=$(jq -nc \
            --arg eval "$MATRIX_EVAL" \
            --arg smoke "$SMOKE_RUN_URL" \
            --arg run "$RUN_URL" \
            '{
              text: "⚠️ Claude Fix Tests cancelled (fix-smoke-failure)",
              blocks: [{
                type: "section",
                text: {
                  type: "mrkdwn",
                  text: ("*⚠️ Claude Fix Tests cancelled*\n\nThe `fix-smoke-failure` job for eval `" + $eval + "` exceeded its 60-minute limit or was cancelled manually.\n\n*Smoke test run:* <" + $smoke + "|View Smoke Test Run>\n*This run:* <" + $run + "|View Claude Run>")
                }
              }]
            }')
          curl -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
